aggressive_definition: No incident aggressive prostate cancer endpoint was analyzed. Tumor aggressiveness was correlated with BMI among men who already had prostate cancer.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: However, there was a direct correlation between BMI and tumor aggressiveness (r = 0.79, P < 0.001).
study_design: Small case-control comparative study of prostate cancer cases and healthy controls.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: A sample of 40 men between 50 and 80 years old were selected for the study: 20 with CaP and 20 healthy men as control group.
reason: Dietary intake was compared between prevalent prostate cancer cases and healthy controls, supporting a general prostate cancer case-control endpoint. The only aggressiveness analysis was a correlation between BMI and tumor aggressiveness among cases; it was not an incident aggressive cancer analysis and did not concern the supplied dietary exposure rows.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Total, saturated, monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fat intake was significantly higher in subjects with CaP; while omega3 fatty acids, vitamin C and lycopene intake was significantly lower than in controls (p < 0.05).
estimate_classifications.reason: The lycopene comparison distinguishes prostate cancer cases from healthy controls but provides no aggressive incident endpoint or effect estimate with a 95% confidence interval.
